questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Being able to speak the local language so as to better delve into the culture and the coutry's opportunities. 
The country not being too close to my home country, since I didn't want to visit my home during the exchange. 
The nature and the people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It can be difficult to find lodgings if you do it privately outside of the host university dorm system - be careful of scammers.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had received help in choosing my courses for the semester and applying online prior to arrival through my host university's international student help centre. There were also cultural introductions to Australia and a student orientation week with lots of activities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's a great way to live closer to the city and find people aside from other international students. The average student is 19-22 years old, so if you're a bit older and fear you might feel out of place in a dorm, I can recommend finding housemates in the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's mainly related to luck/chance. A good way to avoid scammers is to ask if you can pay the rent and bond in cash upon your arrival due to "problems with your bank and international transfers" - someone trying to sell accommodation without actually offering any would not agree to that.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It wasn't entirely transparent, but the support services were great.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Long, especially because you needed language proficiency tests, overseas student health cover etc. But once that was done, everything went smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international student help centre was amazing and very patient.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I could register for all and choose which times I wanted, all in all a great experience.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
1) Check the type of exam/assessment for your unit (some don't have a final exam, which I can recommend). 
2) Try and minimise the amount of days you have to attend university by having two units in the same day or let some be online. 
3) Register/contact the unit as soon as possible - the sooner you do it, the less overwhelmed they will be and the quicker they can help you with whatever issue you might have,

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In my experience, it's rather low level compared to UCPH, but it might depend on the units you take. On the other hand, it's a relief not to be overwhelmed when you're being taught in another language.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two BA courses and two MA courses due to the new/unique perspectives provided in the BA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of handholding - they give you feedback and a lot of guidance on how to write your assignmment. The drawback is that there is less room for creativity/critical thinking/new perspectives.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Bioethics
Culture, society, and health
Leadership
Mindfulness for workplace productivity and well-being.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Global bioethics was really interesting and the most challenging of the courses (without being overwhelming) - it also 

Mindfulness for workplace productivity and well-being was (to my surprise) mainly about developing a mindfulness practice of your own. I found this to be extremely helpful when moving to the other side of the earth, since it helped tackling the issues that it might bring (FOMO, anxiety etc.)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation can get pretty expensive, and the rent is generally very high. 
Coffee and eating out, however, was much cheaper!!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really attend those.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check their website, it's more up to date anyway.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Find a hobby in the city that isn't related to uni (I chose bachata) - it's a great way to meet new, likeminded people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on roadtrips! There's so much in the state of Victoria alone, but visiting other cities is also a great option.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, I look like a local and can speak the language, which was a great advantage.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't really do that - don't be disappointed if the local Australian students don't feel like befriending an  older, international student who's only going to be there for a few months. Find international students or expats/newcomers to the country who want to explore the same things as you instead.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Cafes and bars/clubs close relatively early, which was hard to adjust to in the beginning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How easy it was to attend new events and hobbies as a newcomer to the city - I recommend the apps Eventbrite, Meetup, adn finding acebook groups for travellers or newcomers. You can show up without knowing anyone, and most people will be open to getting to know you.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Consider what you want from the exchange (academic perspective, the dorm life, exploring in the weekend, living on your own, trying new hobbies etc.) and plan your stay accordingly.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the students are young. Think about which campus you take your units at.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, the reinvention of yourself, the exploring.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning, when everything was a bit more uncertain and I hadn't found a group of people that I liked yet.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
